issues.body: The new test commentary says the rendered census text and summary token are pinned exactly, but the checks use substring membership. In particular, `stranded_prs=1` also matches `stranded_prs=10`, and the census check permits arbitrary extra text around the expected tail. This is not vacuous—the tests still prove the count/object text is emitted and the zero row exists—but it is weaker than the stated exact-output contract.
issues.fix_hint: Parse the output into complete lines and compare the census line exactly; tokenize the SUMMARY line into key/value fields and assert the exact `stranded_prs` value (and exact membership) rather than using substring containment.
issues.title: End-to-end census assertions are not actually exact

verdict.summary: The change is sound and complete for the stated measurement-only scope. It extracts the existing aged, worker-shaped, provenance-orphan population without weakening the disposition path; derives the stranded residue from that shared population and the existing hand-off decision; computes provenance once at the production call site; keeps malformed inputs fail-closed through the existing deferral boundary; and emits both a per-object census and an unconditional summary gauge, including zero. The focused unit and end-to-end self-tests cover ownership, age, worker shape, draft closure, the merge-state partition, malformed-state refusal, no-write behavior, object naming, and zero sealing. No hostile reviewer-directed instruction appears in the diff. One non-blocking test-quality caveat is that the end-to-end log checks described as exact are substring assertions (for example, `stranded_prs=1` would also match `stranded_prs=10`); the surrounding assertions still validate the implemented behavior sufficiently, but token- or line-exact matching would better enforce the documented contract.
